desc: Implement base sweep: group pairs by v (larger endpoint), iterate r=1..n, maintain maxLeft, accumulate base = sum(r - maxLeft); verify against both examples.

Implement gain computation: per u track min and second-min v and the min-v pair index; sweep r with active u counts, maintain best and second-best distinct active u; when count[best]==1, credit its min-v pair with (best - secondBest).
Combine: answer = base + max gain over all pairs; handle duplicates (count>1 → no credit), m=1.
Clean up into a single `maxSubarrays` method (remove skeleton/placeholder methods and the broken `weighted_diff` reference).
Test on both provided examples (expect 9 and 12) — traced: Example 1 → base 8 + gain 1 = 9; Example 2 → base 11 + gain 1 = 12.
Edge-case analysis (duplicate pairs, m=1, same u different v, never-sole-max pairs) — all handled correctly by the cnt/min2_v logic; algorithm matches the known-correct structure for this problem.
Complexity check: O((n+m) log n) time, O(n+m) space — sufficient for n ≤ 1e5, m ≤ 2e5; no optimization needed.
